_doc: Byte copies of hermes-home files (card t_29403e19). Never edit the copies; re-vendor and update this pin. tests/hermes_cli/test_fleet_placement_vendored.py checks each sha256 and fails once vendored_at is older than max_age_days. Fork-side differences live in __init__.py (the state root), never in a copy.
source_note: t_77aa2e0e: all five files re-vendored as ONE set from hermes-home main b3a93f3400 (after #11639 482dad6977: admission_demand publishes each demand row's resolved hosts; after #11542 4305794945: alloc_client returns the job_id on a deferred/fallback admit; earlier #11416 4107248b1, FWA B5-P3: the var/placement/exclusions.json read, read_exclusions and EXCLUSIONS_REL are gone, exclusions_path is accepted and ignored; kinds.json pause switches and power_policy added). No subset is coherent: placement calls admission.ceilings and admission_demand.root_directory. All five are byte-equal to hermes-home main at that ref, which also carries fleet_admission 1.0.3 (#11517); the copies track main, not a wheel. The fork cannot depend on that private wheel, so it re-vendors and pins. RUNTIME PRECONDITION (#9789): every ledger/demand/protected-marker write now needs PLACEMENT_ROOT_RECEIPT naming an operator-provisioned receipt for the kanban root, in the dispatcher's environment. load_lines.py, busy_basis.py, fwa.py and fwa_readers.py are not vendored: placement imports each late under ImportError (fleet default line, cpu_busy basis, no fwa hold read); the kanban pause gate reads fwa holds in kanban_pause_hold.
